title: Reading-room site pack
description: Everything a site may change about the shared reading room. Anything not in a pack is the same for every site. roomkit validates packs with this schema plus the checks a schema cannot state (roomkit/pack.py: contrast, CSS scoping, the parity matrix, font files). The host application validates tenant packs against this same file.

site.description: The pack's site; a manifest's site.template names it.

base_url.description: https://host with no path or trailing slash; empty for a site-agnostic pack.

width.description: The width the site's header draws it at (CSS px).

height.description: The height the site's header draws it at (CSS px).

logo.description: The site's header logo, drawn in the home link in place of its text (the text becomes the image's alt).

favicon.description: The site icon: link rel=icon and apple-touch-icon on every page.

backdrop.description: What shows through a transparent page-bg (the site's page color). The contrast check measures against it, and the page paints its body with it.

lang.description: <html lang>, as the site prints it (default en).

theme_color.description: meta theme-color, as the site prints it.

tokens_dark.description: Dark scheme overrides; when present, every color token.

token_notes.description: Why a token's value is what it is, when it is not simply the site's (pack_import.py writes these from the map).

fonts.description: Self-hosted font files in the pack. No CDN.

search_ranking.description: Pagefind's ranking weights for the corpus search (pagefind.options ranking), for a site whose live search ranks differently from Pagefind's defaults. site A: live orders by InnoDB full-text relevance, a term count times IDF squared with no length normalization, so long records rank high there; pageLength 0 and termSaturation 2 come closest (parity-matrix index-fulltext-search).

host.description: The site is a static host with no .htaccess and no nginx, so the build also writes _headers.room, the room's cache policy and CSP as Cloudflare Pages header rules (build.py _pages_headers). The publish script splices it into the site's one root _headers and never ships the fragment. Pages joins a header that two rules set with a comma, so the asset rule detaches the page rule's Cache-Control before setting its own.

nginx.description: The site serves the room from nginx, not Apache: the build also writes .nginx.conf, the .htaccess rules as one location for the site's server block to include (build.py _nginx). root is the directory the mount sits under on the host, outside any WordPress release.

chrome.description: The room's own header, navigation and footer. Text and links only: the look comes from the tokens.

home.description: The site's name in the header, linking to its home page.

tagline.description: A line under the site's name.

skip_text.description: The skip link, the page's first focusable element; it targets #room-content.

nav_label.description: The accessible name of the site navigation (nav aria-label).

menu_label.description: The summary that opens the navigation on narrow screens (details/summary, no JavaScript).

inline_from.description: The viewport width (em) from which the nav's links sit in one row beside the site's name; below it, the Menu button. Measured per site in a browser: the narrowest width where name, gap and the whole link row fit, with margin for font differences.

nav.description: Links, or labelled groups of links (a submenu).

notice.description: A site-wide line under the header.

footer.description: Columns of footer links, each with an optional heading.

footer_text.description: Footer paragraphs (license, disclaimers), verbatim from the site.

source.description: Where the chrome was taken from. Not rendered.

group.description: The group as a label (finder select, jump list), as the site writes it, e.g. "Category".

group_singular.description: Count noun for one group ("1 category").

groups_plural.description: Count noun for any other number of groups ("4 categories").

record_singular.description: Count noun for one record ("1 record").

record_plural.description: Count noun for any other number of records ("5 records").

jump.description: The jump list's visible label ("Jump to jurisdiction:"). The nav's accessible name is this text minus trailing punctuation.

stats_singular.description: Optional: the noun beside the record count in the index header, when the site's header names them differently from its result count (site A: "455 documents" in the header, "455 records" in the count). Defaults to record_singular; set it with stats_plural.

stats_plural.description: Optional: stats_singular's plural. Defaults to record_plural.

fulltext_placeholder.description: The search box placeholder when features.corpus-search is on (it searches record text, not only titles).

newest.description: Optional: the heading of the index's newest-records list (layout.newest). Defaults to "Newest records".

added.description: Optional: the heading of the index's recently added list (layout.added). Defaults to "Recently added".

more_filters.description: Optional: the fold holding the less-used filters (layout.finder compact). Defaults to "More filters".

undated.description: Optional: the adjective for records with no date, in the line a year filter shows (layout.finder compact). Defaults to "undated".

labels.description: Words the room shows. The count nouns are required: the room never builds a plural (no +"s"), it picks singular or plural by the count.

toggle.description: localStorage key of a light/dark toggle shared with the site, or empty for none.

lead.description: The index's order. site (the default): groups and the collections table in the export's order. recent: groups, the group select and the collections table ordered by their newest record (undated groups by their collection's last year), newest first; records within a group keep the export's order; search sits above the collections table.

newest.description: How many of the newest dated records the index lists at the top, under labels.newest. 0 or absent: no list.

added.description: How many of the records most recently added to the catalog (manifest index.added) the index lists beside the newest records, under labels.added, leaving out any already in that list. With both lists, the page shows them as two tabs. 0 or absent: no list.

cover_summaries.description: An index card whose summary is a scan's cover-sheet text (mostly capitals, e.g. FOIA cover sheets): as-exported (the default) shows it; collection-blurb shows the record's collection description from the collections table instead. The record's text is still searched either way.

thumbs.description: Which records the publish step gives a page thumbnail (an exporter step, e.g. a thumbnail writer). lead (the default): the newest and recently added lists only. all: every record with a PDF, so the gallery has pictures.

gallery.description: The index offers a List / Gallery switch (rows layout only). Each card with a thumbnail carries its URL, and no image loads until a visitor picks Gallery; the choice is kept in their browser (localStorage rrIndexView). Hidden without JavaScript. Search results stay a list. Off or absent: no switch, and no byte changes.

page_size.description: Records per page on the index and the facet pages (room-pager.js): numbered Previous / Next controls under the list, over whatever the filters and sort leave showing; the page is in the URL (?page=N). Without JavaScript every record shows. Absent: one page, and no byte changes.

finder.description: The index's filters. plain (the default): every select in a row. compact: the group and year selects shown, the rest under a More filters fold; active filters as removable chips; each option's record count; a line saying how many undated records a year filter hides.

features.description: Surfaces the pack turns on. The template renders a surface only when the pack enables it and the manifest supports it.

collections.description: site A's collections page, collection pages and the index's collections table at their live paths, from the manifest's `collections` block (site_collections.py). Every word and list comes from the export. Off: no collection page, no table, no collections.css or room-collections.js.

machine-text.description: The site's plain-text record index (site A /library/documents.txt) as the exporter wrote it, from the manifest's `machine_text` block (machine_text.py), with a UTF-8 charset in .htaccess. Off: no file, and .htaccess unchanged.

head-meta.description: Each page's <title> and meta tags (description, og:*, article:*, twitter:*) as the site prints them, from the manifest's `head_meta` block (head_meta.py); the room's canonical and JSON-LD stay. A page the block does not name, or any page with the switch off, keeps the room's own head.

topics.description: site A's topics page and every page of every topic (/page/N/ as live) at their live paths, from the manifest's `topics` block (topics.py). Every word, row and paging link comes from the export. Off: no topic page and no topics.css. The in-topic ?s= filter is the site's server's, rendered with features.server-search.

entities.description: The site's entity index and entity pages at their live paths, built from the manifest's `entities` block (entities.py). Every heading, label, count and list comes from the export; nothing is composed. Off: no entity page, no link into one, no entities.css.

page-text.description: Each record with page texts gets <slug>/text/index.html (the text as HTML, one section per page, no JavaScript) and <slug>/<slug>.txt (a UTF-8 download with Page n headers), linked from its record page (page_text.py). Gated records and web snapshots get none. Off: no page, no file, no link, no text.css. Whether the pages are indexed is `page_text.index`.

passage-cite.description: site A's passage citations (passages.py): the reader's Cite page shows each page's exported citation from pages.json with no request; per-hit Cite asks the site's passage route (manifest passages.api) and falls back to the page citation when that fails; curated citations ship as citations.json.

corpus-search.description: A Pagefind index over every record's title, summary, citation, agency, group and page text, built into the room (pagefind/); the finder searches it and suggests from it. Needs the pinned Pagefind (search.py).

facet-pages.description: A page per value of each facet the manifest's site.index.browse names, at <room>/<facet>/<value>/, linked from a browse block on the index: the way to narrow the list without JavaScript (browse.py). Off: no facet page, no browse block, no browse.css.

server-search.description: The site's own search for readers without JavaScript, from the manifest's site.index.server_search (and a topic page's search.param): a plain GET form to the URL the site's server answers (site A /library/?q= and /library/topics/<topic>/?s=, site B /reading-room/?rr_search=). The room answers nothing; after cutover the host must keep sending those queries to the site's server. Off: no such form.

sitemaps.description: sitemap.xml at the room's root: every page the room serves by its live canonical URL (browse.py).

csp-strict.description: The csp policy with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' (build.py CSP_STRICT), for a site whose own deploy audit requires both. Wins over csp. Cost: the no-JS <noscript> PDF object shows its fallback text; the Open/Download links stay.

csp.description: A Content-Security-Policy header in the room's .htaccess (build.py CSP): scripts, workers, frames and connections only from the room's own origin, no plugins beyond the PDF object. Off: no header, as before. Hosts that ignore .htaccess must send the same policy themselves.

web-archive.description: HTML mirror and WACZ snapshot records, rendered by the optional archive reader module.

page_text.description: Settings for features.page-text (D1 of the access-tools plan).

index.description: true: the text pages may be indexed and sit in the sitemap. false, or the key absent: each sends <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> and stays out of the sitemap, because indexed full text makes the people named in a record easier to find.

extra_css.description: An escape hatch, scoped under #room-content (or the page's body.room-plain).

theme.description: The site's WordPress theme, mapped (theme_map.py from packs/<site>/theme.map.json): where the fonts, logo, icon and element styles came from, and the element styles. Written by `roomkit pack-import --theme`, not by hand.

repo.description: The site's parity repo (its directory name).

commit.description: The theme files were read at this commit.

dir.description: The theme's directory in that repo.

page.description: The WordPress page the logo, icon, language and element styles were read from.

css.description: Element styles the theme sets that tokens cannot carry (header band, nav type, table rules), scoped under the room's chrome, content, a11y toolbar or page body.

a11y_toolbar.description: The site's accessibility toolbar, from the wp-accessibility plugin that draws it on the site's WordPress pages: its settings as the page prints them (`var wpatb`), and its stylesheets and icon font, vendored verbatim. The room draws the same markup and sets the same cookies and classes (templates/room/room-a11y.js), so a choice carries between WordPress and the room.

page.description: The WordPress page the settings and files were read from.

wpatb.description: The plugin's settings, as written in the page. Grayscale, a custom location and a custom font-size stylesheet are not ported, so the schema holds them off.

icons_css.description: The plugin's toolbar/fonts/css/a11y-toolbar.css (its icon font's @font-face and classes).

contrast_css.description: The plugin's toolbar/css/a11y-contrast.css, loaded while high contrast is on.

url.description: https://, or a path on the same host.

pack_file.description: A path inside the pack directory.

nav_item.description: A link (label, url) or a labelled group of links (label, links), never both.
